title: Sacrificial protection
caption: A block of zinc bolted to an iron hull corrodes instead of the iron, because zinc (E° −0.76 V) is more easily oxidised than iron (−0.44 V). The electrons it releases flow into the iron, where oxygen is reduced, so the iron is not oxidised.
alt: Seawater with a zinc block connected to iron: zinc is the anode and dissolves; oxygen is reduced at the iron surface.
description: Zinc anode: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻, the zinc corrodes.
Iron, the cathode: O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻; the iron itself is unchanged.
